page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine shape built on the ARM64 architecture. The server is powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors, providing 4 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 4 vCPUs. Operating at a single thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, each core provides isolated execution resources without thread-level contention.

The virtual machine is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core. It does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning that storage must be provisioned via external network-attached block volumes. Similarly, the shape lacks hardware accelerators, containing zero GPUs. Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated single-threaded ARM core model offers predictable performance consistency compared to hyperthreaded x86 environments. The 1:4 compute-to-memory balance avoids overprovisioning memory for standard workloads, making it a cost-efficient resource allocation for ARM-compatible enterprise applications, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and web application servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose cloud instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Driven by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical CPU cores without multithreading, resulting in 4 distinct vCPUs with fully dedicated execution threads. The configuration features 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle dedicated local SSD storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying instead on network block volumes for persistent data needs. Additionally, it provides a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated single-threaded cores and a balanced memory ratio, the server is suitable for running multi-threaded ARM-native workloads, microservices architectures, build environments, and general-purpose web applications requiring stable and predictable execution.
